results.title: What It Actually Costs to Rent an H100, H200, or B200 in October 2026
results.author: Dex Mareno
highlights:
After a summer of falling floors, October pauses: H100 ~$2/hr, H200 ~$3+, the B200 in-stock floor flat near $3.75 — but a typical on-demand B200 now rents at ~$8. The floor stopped falling.

 By Dex Mareno · claude-sonnet · October 23, 2026 

The takeaway

- As of late October 2026, the cheapest reliable on-demand H100 (80GB) is back around $1.99/GPU-hr (Voltage Park), with brand-name specialty clouds at ~$2.50 (Hyperstack PCIe), ~$2.89 (RunPod), and ~$2.90 SXM (Ori); the median 'cheapest' across two dozen providers is ~$3.33, and spot dips to ~$0.94 (Prime Intellect). Hyperscaler H100 is still ~$10–13/hr.
- H200 (141GB) firmed since September: neocloud floors run ~$3.14–3.99 (Prime Intellect ~$3.14, Spheron ~$3.35, Theta ~$3.69, Hyperbolic ~$3.99), the Ornn transacted index settled at $5.24 on Oct 12, and getdeploying's on-demand median is ~$5.00 across 33 providers. Spot ~$2.29. Hyperscaler H200 is ~$7.91–13.78.
- B200 (Blackwell) is the split-screen card: the verified in-stock on-demand floor is ~$3.75 (Packet.ai, per getdeploying on Oct 22) — essentially flat versus September's ~$3.70 — but the on-demand MEDIAN is now ~$7.99–8.19 (RunPod $7.99, Together $8.19). Spot from ~$3.20 (Vultr).
- The October story is that the floor stopped falling: after a summer of monthly cuts, floors across all three cards are flat-to-firmer.
- And the spread that matters moved inside the specialty market — the ~2× gap between a marketplace in-stock rate and a brand-name neocloud's on-demand list price is now sharper than the old specialty-vs-hyperscaler framing for anyone who can tolerate the availability risk.
- The decision is still utilization, not sticker: below ~40–50% duty cycle a per-token API almost always beats renting metal.

...

| GPU | Cheapest reliable on-demand | Typical on-demand (median) | Hyperscaler on-demand | Best for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 (80GB) | ~$1.99/hr (Voltage Park), ~$2.50 PCIe (Hyperstack) | ~$3.33/hr | ~$10–13/hr | 70B-class inference, most fine-tunes |
| H200 (141GB) | ~$3.14/hr (Prime Intellect), ~$3.35 (Spheron) | ~$5.00–5.24/hr | ~$7.91–13.78/hr | Bigger context, larger models on one card |
| B200 (Blackwell) | ~$3.75/hr in-stock (Packet.ai) | ~$7.99–8.19/hr | ~$14–16/hr | Frontier-size inference, heavy training |
| GB200 / B300 | ~$8/hr and up, much is quote-only | varies widely | ~$16–27/hr | Largest models, frontier training |
| Spot / preemptible | ~$0.94/hr H100, ~$2.29 H200, ~$3.20 B200 | no SLA | rarely offered | Interruptible batch jobs |

...

## The price map (published on-demand rates, late October 2026)#

Every figure below is a published on-demand rate, gathered the last week of October 2026 from public pricing pages and multi-provider trackers (getdeploying, Ornn, gpuperhour, Spheron, and vendor pages). GPU pricing moves weekly with supply, region, and commitment — read this for the shape of the market, then confirm on the provider's own page before you commit a dollar.

- H100 (80GB) — the workhorse, and steady. The cheapest reliable on-demand rate is back near $1.99/hr (Voltage Park), with ~$2.50 PCIe at Hyperstack, ~$2.89 at RunPod, and ~$2.90 SXM at Ori. The median "cheapest across providers" is ~$3.33. Spot dips near $0.94/hr (Prime Intellect). Hyperscaler on-demand: ~$10–13/hr — the same card, 5–6× the money.
- H200 (141GB) — more memory, and firmer than September. Neocloud floors run ~$3.14–3.99/hr (~$3.14 Prime Intellect, ~$3.35 Spheron, ~$3.69 Theta, ~$3.99 Hyperbolic). The Ornn transacted index — settled daily from real neocloud deals — printed $5.24 on Oct 12, and getdeploying's on-demand median is ~$5.00 across 33 providers. Spot ~$2.29. Hyperscaler H200 runs ~$7.91–13.78 (Thunder Compute: AWS ~$7.91–9.89, Azure ~$10.60–13.78).
- B200 (Blackwell, 180GB) — the split-screen card. The cheapest verified in-stock on-demand rate is ~$3.75/hr (Packet.ai, per getdeploying on Oct 22) — essentially flat versus September's ~$3.70. But the on-demand median is now ~$7.99–8.19: RunPod lists $7.99/hr and Together ~$8.19/hr. Spot from ~$3.20 (Vultr). Hyperscaler B200 is ~$14–16/hr.
- GB200 / B300 — the Grace-Blackwell superchips remain premium and partly quote-only: roughly $8/hr and up where published, ~$16–27 at the hyperscalers. If you need one, you're negotiating, not shopping a list.

...

1. The floor stopped falling. H100's reliable on-demand floor held near $2 (and the brand-name cheap number, ~$2.50–2.90, is a touch firmer). The B200 in-stock floor is flat at ~$3.75. For the first monthly map all year, the cheap end didn't get cheaper.
2. H200 firmed. Neocloud floors moved up from ~$2.30 in September to ~$3.14–3.99, and the transacted index sits at $5.24. If you were waiting for the H200 to drift down to the H100's price, that's not happening this month.
3. The spread moved inside the specialty market. The gap that defined the summer was specialty-vs-hyperscaler (still a real 5–7×). The sharper gap now is floor-vs-median within the neoclouds: a B200 in-stock marketplace rate (~$3.75) versus a named neocloud's on-demand list (~$8) is a ~2× difference — and the cheap number comes with availability and trust caveats the expensive one doesn't.

results.title: Lambda announces GPU price rises of about 15% — B200, H100 and A100 80GB, from Nov 16 | GPUJournal
highlights:
# Lambda announces GPU price rises of about 15% — B200, H100 and A100 80GB, from Nov 16

Nov 6, 2026

Read on Lambda's own pricing page today, Nov 6, 2026: the Instances table now prints the prices that take effect on Nov 16, 2026 — HGX B200 up $1.00 an hour, H100 up $0.60 and A100 80GB up $0.40. It is the largest single announced rise we have caught this autumn, and renters have ten days' notice.

Image: GPUJournal price record — read on lambda.ai/pricing

What was announced, in the pricing page's own words (read Nov 6, 2026): 'These prices take effect November 16, 2026, at 00:00 UTC. Until then, log in to your Lambda Cloud account to see current pricing.' The printed Nov 16 rates: HGX B200 $7.69 an hour (from the $6.69 last verified on Nov 5, +14.9%), HGX H100 $4.59 (from $3.99, +15.0%), HGX A100 80GB $3.19 (from $2.79, +14.3%), and HGX A100 40GB unchanged at $1.99. Lambda is also now at a new address — lambda.com — announced on its blog on Nov 5, 2026; the pricing page itself still answers at lambda.ai/pricing.

How we are treating it: an announced rise is not a live price. Our board keeps Lambda's last verified rates until Nov 16 and will move only when the new rates are re-verified in effect on or after that date — the rise is recorded in Price Watch today as announced, with both dates. One consequence of the announcement is already live, though: Lambda's currently-effective rates can no longer be read on its public page, only after logging in, so today's public check could verify the future rates but not re-read the current ones.

What it does to the board when it lands: Lambda's B200 at $6.69 is currently the cheapest verified HGX B200 instance rate we list from a self-serve cloud; at $7.69 it would sit above RunPod Community's $5.98 marketplace rate and just below RunPod Secure's $7.99. Its H100 at $4.59 would remain above the board's best H100 SXM offer (TensorDock, from $2.25 at an 8-GPU minimum) but move Lambda from the middle of the H100 pack toward its top. Around-the-clock, the announced rises add about $730 a month per B200, $438 per H100 and $292 per A100 80GB on a 730-hour month.

results.title: GPU Cloud Pricing Index, November 2026: H100 to B300
highlights:
- November 4, 2026

...

Every month we check the public on-demand prices of specialist GPU clouds to set our own: CoreGPU prices every GPU at least 25% below the market median. This is the data behind that number, as listed on November 4, 2026.

## Method

- One on-demand price per provider and GPU, taken from public pricing pages or price APIs. Prices for 8-GPU nodes are divided by eight.
- Specialist GPU clouds only for the median. Hyperscalers (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle) are listed separately because their prices are 2.5 to 4.5 times higher.
- Monthly cost = hourly price × 730 hours. Prices exclude taxes.

## Median prices by GPU

| GPU | Prices found | Lowest $/h | Median $/h | Median / month |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NVIDIA B300 | 8 | 6.60 | 8.98 | $6,552 |
| NVIDIA B200 | 11 | 5.43 | 8.19 | $5,979 |
| NVIDIA H200 | 12 | 2.90 | 4.94 | $3,606 |
| NVIDIA H100 SXM | 16 | 1.99 | 3.72 | $2,716 |
| NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 | 9 | 1.40 | 2.19 | $1,599 |
| NVIDIA L40S | 11 | 0.73 | 1.57 | $1,146 |
| AMD MI325X | 2 | 3.80 | 4.21 | $3,071 |
| AMD MI300X | 4 | 2.59 | 3.22 | $2,351 |

The lowest prices often come from marketplaces with variable host quality or from “starting at” prices that are rarely available. The median is a better picture of what a team actually pays for reliable capacity.

...

## Hyperscalers

On-demand prices per GPU-hour at the largest clouds remain far above specialist clouds: H100 from $6.88 (8-GPU instance divided by eight) to more than $12 depending on the provider, and B300 from $15 to $17.80. Commitments of one to three years cut those prices by 30 to 56%.

## What moved in 2026

- Prices are rising again for flagships. At least one large specialist cloud announced increases of 10 to 26% on H100, H200 and B300 from December 1.
- Clusters cost more than single instances. Multi-node offers are commonly 20 to 50% more per GPU than on-demand single servers.
- Listed is not available. Several providers list GPUs with no deployable region, or “contact sales” for every flagship.
- Fees moved to storage and idle time. Egress is mostly free; stopped-instance storage, public IPs and minimum billing periods are where extra cost appears.

results.title: RunPod Secure Cloud GPU Rates Rise: H100 $3.99, B200 $7.99
results.author: TSN Newsroom
highlights:
# RunPod’s Secure Cloud GPU Rates Have Risen: H100 SXM Now $3.99 an Hour, B200 $7.99, a Tracker Reports

October 10, 2026

Illustration.

A GPU price tracker, GPU Economy, says RunPod raised 12 of its 29 on-demand Secure Cloud GPU rates on 8 October 2026 [1]. RunPod’s pricing page now shows the higher prices [2]. RunPod made no announcement that we could find, so the timing and the old prices rest on the tracker.

## The new rates

RunPod sells two tiers, Secure Cloud and Community Cloud; on its listings the Community rates are lower. Prices are in US dollars per GPU per hour, on demand, meaning pay as you go. GPU Economy reports [1]:

| GPU | Before | Now | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 SXM | $3.49 | $3.99 | +14.3% |
| H200 | $4.59 | $5.29 | +15.3% |
| B200 | $6.79 | $7.99 | +17.7% |
| B300 | $7.89 | $8.99 | +13.9% |

The H100, H200, B200 and B300 are Nvidia data-centre chips used to train and run AI models. The tracker says the 12 rises came “between our reads of October 8, 2026 at 15:41 and 16:41 UTC”, which is 16:41 and 17:41 in London. It also computes that one H100 SXM running for a 730-hour month went from $2,547.70 to $2,912.70.

## What did not change

The tracker says “None of the 35 Community Cloud on-demand rates changed in the same read”: the H100 SXM there stayed at $2.69 and the B200 at $5.98 [1].

## What RunPod’s page shows

RunPod’s pricing page lists $3.99/hr for the H100 SXM, $7.99/hr for the B200, $5.29/hr for the H200 and $8.99/hr for the B300 [2]. But the page is labelled “Updated September 27, 2026”, which does not match the tracker’s 8 October timing. The page’s hidden structured data, the code search engines read, still lists the old Secure Cloud prices, such as $3.49 for the H100 SXM [2]. The tracker says it read RunPod’s public API, and that on 9 October the page’s own markup still carried $3.49 [1]. That fits what we see.

## What this does not show

- A RunPod announcement. We found none, and no reason for the rises.
- When RunPod made the change. The tracker reads hourly and gives a one-hour window.
- Other providers’ prices. This covers RunPod only.
- Every region or product. Serverless and cluster pricing are not covered.

### One Big Thing · Phase 3 · Compute

What happened: Nebius raised on-demand GPU prices on October 1, its second hike in about three months. Independent trackers show the same direction across the market.

Why it matters: The bear case on AI infrastructure assumed GPUs lose value fast. Rental rates are the cleanest test of that assumption, and so far the test is failing.

By the numbers:

- Nebius list price for an H100 went from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU-hour; B300 from $7.85 to $9.50.
- The Ornn H100 index settled at $3.17 on October 23, up about 4% in a month.

results.title: Nebius moves spare GPU hours to spot prices | Wire
results.author: Sean
highlights:
Nebius switched its spare GPU hours from a fixed price to live spot pricing on 8 October. An H100 hour now floats between $0.79 and $4.49. Nebius gets paid more when clusters are full. The stuck step is the idle hour, and only the console shows it.

...

Nebius no longer sells its spare GPU hours at a fixed price. Since 8 October 2026, its interruptible (preemptible) GPU hours float. An H100 hour now costs anywhere from $0.79 to $4.49. Until last week it was a flat $2.15. The price moves with how full Nebius's clusters are, and it can change every 15 minutes. On the neocloud model, this is the idle-hour step: Nebius now gets paid more for spare chips when they are scarce, and less when they sit.

## What happened

Nebius, the GPU cloud that rents Nvidia chips by the hour, updated its compute price list for October. Two changes, a week apart:

8 October

Preemptible B300, B200, H200, H100 and RTX PRO 6000 hours move to dynamic spot pricing

Nebius Compute pricing documentation

The band

Floor of $0.79 (H100, H200) or $0.99 (B200, B300). Ceiling one cent below the on-demand rate

Price set by capacity, cluster use, customer demand and pricing preferences

1 October

On-demand rates up 17% to 21%: H100 $3.85 to $4.50, B300 $7.85 to $9.50

This raised the spot ceiling too, since the ceiling tracks on-demand

Who can see the price

Current and past spot prices sit inside the Nebius console, not on a public page

...

Sources: Nebius, Compute pricing in Nebius AI Cloud, read 9 Oct 2026: from 1 Oct 2026 on-demand H100 $4.50 (was $3.85), H200 $5.40 (was $4.50), B200 $8.50 (was $7.15), B300 $9.50 (was $7.85); from 8 Oct 2026 preemptible pricing for B300, B200, H200, H100 and RTX PRO 6000 switches to dynamic spot pricing, preemptible from $0.79 (H100, H200, RTX PRO 6000) and from $0.99 (B200, B300), previously fixed at $2.15 (H100), $2.45 (H200), $3.95 (B200), $4.30 (B300) and $0.95 (RTX PRO 6000); spot prices can change as often as every 15 minutes and the highest is one cent below the on-demand rate; Nebius price page, read 9 Oct 2026: commitment discounts of up to 35% off on-demand for multi-month cluster reservations, current spot prices shown in the Nebius console; GPU Cloud Advisors, 28 Sep 2026: 1 Oct increase of 17% to 21%. The monthly server cost examples, the ceilings as a multiple of the old price, and the spread are our arithmetic. Not investment advice. Do your own research.
